methodological_questions: How is offensive reorganization measured, and what is L (the baseline against which it is measured)?
Is the reorganization measure computed independently of the PPP outcome, or derived from the same possessions?
Does the spell-level sample of 148 have enough power to detect a plausible effect, given the stated MDE placeholder (rho not specified)?
Are play-type labels accurate enough to support a reorganization measure?
How are regression to the mean, lineup and opponent confounding, and playoff/regular-season differences handled?

historical_evidence.finding: Connector absence displaced team offensive identity (D_A) more than usage-matched non-organizer absence: unmatched 0.2020 vs 0.1021 (t=5.97, p=2.87e-08); usage-matched paired dD_A +0.1151, P(conn>ctrl)=81.2%, n=96; vs terminal +0.0777, p=0.0261, n=25. Recorded limitation: small_sample; mechanical_floor risk.

Adapt-vs-continue matched-pair overall-offense excess (post-hoc). Caliper 0.10: group A excess +0.076 [+0.068,+0.084] n=3421; group B excess +0.014 [-0.019,+0.046] n=255 (p=0.386); gap B-A = -0.062. Group B CIs include 0 at all calipers except 0.15. Recorded as a reconstructed post-hoc cohort, not a validated sample.

Play-type replacement similarity vs absorb/cascade: mean similarity ABSORBED +0.863 vs CASCADE +0.848; Spearman(sim, -gap) = -0.19 (wrong-signed). Recorded failure type B_powered_null, but the sample and power were not recorded; verdict null.

Play-type label accuracy audit overall FAIL: OTHER 20.2% vs <10% target; 40.8% low confidence; DRIVE foul-draw 1.7% vs 14-22% benchmark; most play types have PPP above benchmark band; MIA identity checks fail. Verdict tool_eval_fail.

Defensive in-game adaptation to repeated play type. League-wide within-game slope -0.0019 PPP/exposure (SE 0.0019); across-game +0.0004 (SE 0.0015). Only PULL_UP survives Holm (B -0.0243, SE 0.0061, holm 0.0004). Team-trait split-half r +0.008; season-to-season +0.037. Limited by insufficient_exposure, label error, low measurement reliability.

Defensive scheme change inferred from labels: within-game change 61.0%, cross-game change 67.7%; transition matrices near-uniform. The record states the inferred label cannot separate real defensive adjustment from offense executing differently, and that near-uniform matrices are consistent with label noise.

BEST-vs-continue gap after a slump was +0.248 (SE 0.009), the same without a slump (+0.239) and under a fixed CUT-heavy ranking (+0.238). The recorded verdict is artifact_found, with the gap attributed to construction rather than to the slump.
Route entropy: shaper presence on non-focal play-type entropy d = -0.0455 (n_ts=80); organizer +0.0115. No CI reported; the paper reads this as rebalancing rather than expansion. Verdict null.

Memoryless Monte Carlo generative check: uncalibrated PPP std 1.149 vs simulated 1.152; lag-1 scoring autocorrelation real -0.0022 vs simulated +0.0029. Described as an existence proof, not independent evidence.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Matched-pair comparison of adapt vs continue groups on overall-offense excess, using a post-hoc reconstructed group B
failed_approaches.why: Group B CI includes 0 at the primary caliper (p=0.386, n=255 pairs / 242 games); the group is post-hoc and not a validated successful-adaptation sample; recorded as A_unanswerable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using play-type replacement similarity to separate absorption from cascade after a player sits
failed_approaches.why: Similarity did not separate the groups and the sign was wrong; recorded as B_powered_null, though sample size and power were not recorded and label error is flagged.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferred play-type labels as a basis for adaptation findings
failed_approaches.why: Audit failed: OTHER share 20.2%, foul-draw rates far below benchmark, PPP above band for most types, identity checks failing; recorded as C_artifact and tool_eval_fail.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Within-game exposure slope of PPP to repeated play type
failed_approaches.why: Effect is near zero overall; only one play type survives correction; team-trait reliability is low; limited by insufficient exposure and label error.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferred defensive scheme-change transitions from play-type labels
failed_approaches.why: Label cannot separate defensive adjustment from offensive execution; near-uniform transitions consistent with label noise; recorded as A_unanswerable.

evidence_establishes: Connector absence, as a player-identity measure, changes team offensive identity more than usage-matched absence of non-organizers (FAM:SF-APPS-088, supported, n=96 matched pairs). This is an identity-displacement result, not a PPP-change result.
Play-type labels from this pipeline have documented accuracy failures (FAM:SF-APPM-014), so any reorganization measure built on them inherits label error.

Earlier attempts to link play-type or similarity-based reorganization to outcomes (FAM:SF-CHT-052, FAM:SF-APPS-025, FAM:SF38, FAM:SF-PAP-008) returned null, untestable, or inconclusive results, with several limited by power, label quality, or post-hoc cohort construction.
Small-sample and label-quality caveats recur across the retrieved families, so the group-level question has not been answered by this project.
evidence_does_not_establish: None of the returned records measures offensive reorganization relative to a baseline L, or regresses change in PPP on such a measure after player absence.
No returned record reports a PPP-change outcome for absence spells; SF-APPS-088 reports identity displacement, not scoring change.
Whether a reorganization effect exists at the 148-spell scale, and at what magnitude, is not established.
The meaning of L and the definition of reorganization are not stated in the retrieved evidence or the task statement.
own_inferences: The research question as posed is underspecified: L, the reorganization metric, the PPP-change window, and the absence definition are not defined, so it cannot be tested as written.
A reorganization measure built from play-type possessions and PPP change measured on the same possessions would create outcome-derived labelling and leakage risk.
With 148 spells, power to detect a modest effect is likely low unless the expected effect is large; the MDE is recorded only as a placeholder with rho unspecified.
Unit counts are ambiguous: n=986 and 148 spells are not clearly linked; the 148-spell figure is the likely effective sample.
uncertainties: Definition of L and the reorganization metric are missing.
MDE value and the rho parameter are unspecified; power cannot be computed from the stated information.
Relationship between n=986 and n=148 spells is not stated.
Partial 2025-26 data (regular season and playoffs) is not yet complete on the decision date; including it would change the sample.
Label accuracy for the 2022-23 to 2025-26 play-type files has not been validated beyond the failed audit in FAM:SF-APPM-014.
Whether the retrieval set is complete for this project's earlier work is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieved evidence shows that play-type-based similarity and reorganization-style measures have produced null, untestable, or artifact results, and that play-type labels fail audit (FAM:SF-CHT-052, FAM:SF-APPS-025, FAM:SF-APPM-014, FAM:SF38, FAM:SF-APPA-005). Together with the undefined L and the 148-spell sample, this moved the decision from a provisional proceed to do_not_proceed as posed. A test is still possible if the measure and L are fixed in advance and labels are validated.

blocking_constraints.text: Play-type labels failed audit (OTHER 20.2%, foul-draw 1.7% vs 14-22%); reorganization measured from them is unreliable.
If reorganization and PPP change are computed from the same possessions, the predictor partly encodes the outcome.
148 spells with an unspecified MDE (rho) gives unknown and probably low power to detect a modest effect.
Team-trait and season-to-season reliability of play-type measures is low in related work (split-half r +0.008, season-to-season +0.037 in FAM:SF38).

prior_work.summary: No retrieved study measures offensive reorganization relative to L and regresses PPP change on it. Related work covers identity displacement after connector absence (supported, FAM:SF-APPS-088), play-type similarity and adaptation (null, untestable, or inconclusive: FAM:SF-CHT-052, FAM:SF-APPS-025, FAM:SF38), and label audits that failed (FAM:SF-APPM-014). The question is therefore not answered, but adjacent work exists.

risks.text: Play-type labels fail audit; OTHER share and foul-draw rates are far from benchmark; reorganization from these labels is biased.
Reorganization and PPP change may be built from the same possessions, so the predictor leaks the outcome.
Using post-absence possessions to define the reorganization baseline L, or to select spells, leaks future information into the predictor.
148 spells and an unspecified MDE; power to detect a modest effect is probably low.
Spells selected because of an extreme PPP drop or reorganization spike will regress toward the mean, inflating apparent effects.
Opponent quality, lineup, rest, usage, injury status and garbage time may drive both reorganization and PPP change.
Some players or teams have few absence spells, so team-level estimates are unstable.
Related families show low reliability of play-type and team-trait measures.
Frequency of absences and the baseline PPP differ across seasons and playoffs, so pooling may mix regimes.
Pooling 2022-23 through 2025-26 may mix rule and pace changes across seasons.
A post-hoc cohort construction, as in FAM:SF-APPS-025, could produce an apparent effect that depends on the placebo or caliper choice.
Multiple measures of reorganization, windows, and L values invite selective reporting.
Joining play-by-play, substitution intervals, and derived play-type records across sources could misalign possessions.

design.estimand: Among player-absence spells, the association between offensive reorganization relative to a pre-specified baseline L and the change in PPP from the pre-absence to the post-absence window. The primary parameter is the regression slope of PPP change on the standardized reorganization index.
design.unit: Player-absence spell (one row per spell, with team-level possessions aggregated within the spell window).
design.sample: Spells from 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons only, with 2025-26 limited to the complete regular season (from 2026-04-13). Playoffs and partial 2025-26 data are excluded from the primary analysis and reported separately. Reconcile n=986 versus 148 spells before analysis.
design.power: Not computable from the stated information. Before analysis, fix rho and the MDE, then compute power for the spell count. If power is below 0.8 at the pre-specified MDE, report the result as inconclusive rather than null.
design.controls: Opponent defensive rating, lineup and starter identity, minutes and usage of the absent player, rest days, home/away, garbage-time filter, season fixed effects, and team fixed effects. Reorganization is computed from a separate possession set from the PPP outcome (split-sample or time-disjoint windows) to avoid outcome-derived labels.
design.falsification: Placebo absences of low-impact bench players; pre-absence window as a placebo outcome; a shuffled reorganization index within team-season; and a label-validation check that the play-type audit passes its thresholds before the measure is used.
design.multiplicity: One primary test (slope of PPP change on the pre-registered reorganization index at the pre-registered L). Secondary measures are reported with Holm correction; any alternative L or window is exploratory only.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the primary slope's 95% CI excludes zero in the pre-registered direction, the placebo tests show no effect, and power at the MDE is at least 0.8. Rejected if the CI is within the pre-registered null range and power is adequate. Otherwise report as uncertain.
design.data_version: Lock the 2026-11-01 snapshot for all files; record the 2025-26 regular-season completion status; log play-type audit results before analysis.

research_concepts: offensive reorganization relative to baseline L
methodological_questions: Does offensive reorganization relative to L predict change in points per possession following player absence?
What sample size and minimum detectable effect are needed given n=148 spells?
How should reorganization be measured reliably from play-by-play and play-type data?
Are there leakage, regression-to-the-mean, or confounding risks when the outcome change is derived from the same possessions as the reorganization measure?
args.query: player absence offensive reorganization relative to L change in points per possession spells play-type initiator

You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:

The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
